Namespace frontier and continuation checks retain one exact generation witness throughout preparation.
New hosted graph, sparse and HBC metadata roots use native namespaces; existing LSM roots retain authority.
Native ordinary text insertion/deletion and prepared multi-segment sets use atomic artifact/metadata activation, preserving replay checkpoints.
Logical namespace snapshots retain data frontiers and reject allocator inspection; full inspection snapshots retain metadata fences.
Revision 14 fences older graph/vector implementations while preserving revision-13 decoding and the existing atomic owner migration protocol.
The mixed-index handoff regression now exercises an actual range-backed text artifact rather than depending on removed graph SST files.
